title: Artificial Intelligence in Intelligent Tutoring Robots: A Systematic Review and Design Guidelines
extended_summary:
This paper reviews recent advances in the design of intelligent tutoring robots (ITRs) and surveys how artificial intelligence techniques are being used in these systems. Rather than testing a specific intervention with learners, it organizes the field around a relationship model of teaching and learning and then maps that model onto a perception-planning-action architecture for robot tutors.

The paper argues that effective tutoring robots must support three broad functions: perceiving students and their context, planning instruction based on student models, and acting through multi-modal communication and scene construction. It discusses AI methods for multi-modal sensing, learning style and knowledge mastery analysis, student modeling, decision making, and generating virtual or physical tutoring environments.

The intended context is AI-assisted education, especially intelligent tutoring robots that may interact with students, curriculum, and social milieu. The conclusions are primarily conceptual: the authors provide design guidelines, identify promising AI techniques, and highlight open research problems such as multi-modal data fusion, explainable student modeling, multi-objective decision making, and more mature embodied robot tutoring.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review and design-guidelines paper, not an empirical evaluation of an intervention. It does not report a study design with causal identification or primary outcome data for K-12 learners.
impact_tier_rationale: No impact estimate is reported because the paper synthesizes prior work and proposes a framework rather than measuring learning or implementation outcomes itself.

interventions.use_case: Systematic review of intelligent tutoring robots that use multi-modal sensing, student modeling, decision-making, and embodied/virtual communication to support teaching and learning.
